result.target_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Reporting
result.target_summary: Citi adopted Accounting Standards Update No. 2023-07, which improves reportable segment disclosures, on a retrospective basis for the annual period ending December 31, 2024, and on a current basis for the interim period beginning January 1, 2025. The adoption includes disclosing significant segment expenses provided to the CODM, the CODM's title and position, and an explanation of how the CODM assesses segment performance.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures concern the adoption of ASU No. 2023-07, Segment Reporting (Topic 280). The 2023 disclosure describes the issuance of the ASU and the required retrospective adoption for the annual period ending Dec 31, 2024. The 2024 disclosure confirms the adoption of this same ASU for the annual period ending Dec 31, 2024, detailing the specific enhanced disclosures (significant segment expenses, CODM title/position, etc.).

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of New Segment Reporting Standard
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation adopted the Financial Accounting Standards Board's amended segment reporting requirements effective January 1, 2024, on a retrospective basis, to include disclosures of incremental segment expense categories as detailed in Note 23.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America adopted the FASB's segment reporting amendments (ASU 2023-07) retrospectively for the fiscal year 2024 to enhance disclosures regarding significant segment expenses and the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM). Citi adopted the ASU effective for the annual period ending December 31, 2024 and interim periods beginning January 1, 2025, requiring disclosure of significant segment expenses regularly provided to the CODM. Bank of America adopted the guidance effective January 1, 2024, on a retrospective basis, specifically to include disclosures of incremental segment expense categories.

sentences.text: In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2023-07, Segment Reporting (Topic 280): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures, intended to improve reportable segments disclosure requirements primarily through enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses.
Citi adopted the ASU on a retrospective basis for its annual period ending December 31, 2024 and the ASU for the interim period beginning January 1, 2025.
The Financial Accounting Standards Board amended the segment reporting requirements to add disclosures of incremental segment expense categories.
The Corporation adopted this guidance effective January 1, 2024 on a retrospective basis.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Disclosures
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2024 (interim periods starting January 2025), the firm adopted ASU No. 2023-07 under a retrospective approach, requiring enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses; adoption had no impact on financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs adopted ASU No. 2023-07 retrospectively to enhance reportable segment disclosures, primarily regarding significant segment expenses provided to the CODM. Citi adopted the standard for the annual period ending December 31, 2024 and interim periods starting January 1, 2025. Goldman Sachs adopted it for annual periods beginning January 2024 and interim periods beginning January 2025. Both disclosures note that the adoption relates to enhanced disclosure requirements for segment expenses and CODM assessment methods without impacting financial results.

This ASU became effective for the firm for annual periods beginning in January 2024, and is effective for interim periods beginning in January 2025 under a retrospective approach.
